capacity_gross_kwh.notes: GM TechLink: the 2020 pack is 66 kWh "up from 60 kWh in previous model years" (Bolt EV 2017-2019). Wikipedia lists 60 kWh for 2017-2019 too. Bare nominal capacity, treated as gross.

capacity_usable_kwh.notes: Estimated: GM states only 60 kWh (nominal). Applied the 65/66 usable-to-nominal ratio of the 2020-23 pack of the same LG cell family (66 kWh GM nominal per GM TechLink; 65 kWh per the 2022 GM figure relayed by InsideEVs): 60 x 65/66 = 59.1. Korea's ministry measured 60.9 kWh (not opened). WEAK: the 65/66 pair is a press nominal, not a published usable ratio, and the N2.1 chemistry differs from N2.2.

chemistry.notes: Estimated: Wikipedia: first-generation Bolt uses a "nickel-rich lithium-ion" pack (LG Chem cells); GM calls the 2017-19 chemistry N2.1 (GM TechLink). Closest enum nmc.

nominal_voltage_class.notes: Estimated: ArenaEV: "Liquid-cooled Li-ion 350V" (a 350 V nominal pack is the 400 V class). Page covers the 2019/2020 66 kWh car; 2017-19 uses the same cell stack count and architecture.

preconditioning.notes: Estimated: InsideEVs on the previous Bolt: "The lack of preconditioning meant charging in the dead of winter took even longer." No battery-warming feature found for 2017-2023 Bolt EV/EUV; GM's automatic preconditioning arrived with Google built-in nav on the Ultium cars.

dc_max_kw.notes: Estimated: Torque News: 2020 tops out at 55 kW, "the same rate familiar to anyone fast charging a previous model year"; Wikipedia: first generation 55 kW SAE Combo DC (optional; tapers to 38 kW at 56 % and 24 kW at 68 %). Other sources say 50 kW. DC fast charging was a factory option on the 2017-2020 cars (standard on the 2021 Premier and from 2022).

ac_max_kw.notes: Wikipedia: Level 2 initially up to 7.2 kW (32 A), raised to 11.5 kW with the 2022 refresh. ArenaEV lists 11 kW and Recharged 7.7 kW for 2017-2021 (conflict).
